evals.prompt: I'm running PratoConf, a two-day single-track community conference. 650 tickets sold; our registrations person, who tracks this closely, projects 480 will actually turn up based on past editions. We also have 40 volunteers, 12 organizers, 25 speakers and about 10 sponsor booth staff on site. The registration form collected dietary info from ticket holders: 38 vegetarian, 12 vegan, 6 gluten-free, 3 nut allergies. The main hall is standing room only - no seated capacity for the crowd - and the venue allows outside caterers but bans chafing dishes and open flame. Lunch gap is 60 minutes. What format should we feed people in, and how many meals do I tell the caterer?
evals.expected_output: A service-style recommendation (individually packaged labelled meals) sized from the expected-show-up figure with the buffer named separately, dietary counts flagged incomplete and re-collected from every population fed, family-style deleted on the equipment ban, and the service window handed off as a requirement.
expectations: The meal order is based on the 480 expected-show-up figure, not the 650 registration count.
The 170-person gap between registrations and expected show-up is named separately as a buffer, not silently folded into the order or dropped.
The response does not derive its own attendance or no-show estimate; it takes the projected 480 as the number to feed.
The dietary counts are flagged as incomplete because they were collected only from ticket holders.
Volunteers, organizers, speakers and sponsor booth staff are named as populations whose dietary needs must be collected before the order is placed.
Dietary count collection is sequenced before the service style is finalized or the order placed.
Family-style shared platters are removed from consideration entirely because of the chafing-dish and open-flame ban, not merely ranked lower.
Plated per-guest service is ruled out on the grounds that the room has no seated capacity for the whole population.
Individually packaged labelled meals are recommended as the service style.
Any buffet option discussed is conditioned on posted allergen labelling; an unlabelled buffet is never offered as a cheaper variant.
No per-head food cost, per-person quantity ratio, or invented price figure appears in the answer.
The needed service window is handed to whoever owns the schedule as a requirement; the 60-minute lunch slot is not moved or lengthened.
The response asks for or defers to the event's committed dietary-category list instead of treating the four registration-form categories as the complete commitment.

evals.prompt: Evening of day one at DevHarbor Summit, 300 attendees. The board is split two ways. Option A: cash bar - our treasurer says it's the lowest-liability choice since attendees buy their own drinks and we're not the ones serving. Option B: Kafelog, a monitoring vendor, has offered to fully fund an unlimited open bar with their branding on it, which would cost us nothing. We haven't booked the evening venue yet - we'll do that next week once the bar question settles. Which option should we take?
evals.expected_output: Both options rejected as framed: the cash bar's liability claim corrected, the uncapped open bar refused even sponsor-funded, and a bounded hosted service (or dry posture) designed with a cap mechanism, a named cap holder, equal alcohol-free provision, and the decision fixed before the venue is booked.
expectations: The treasurer's claim is corrected: the cash bar is identified as carrying the highest compliance cost of the alcohol postures, not the lowest.
The reason given is that selling alcohol is commonly a separate permission from serving it, sitting with whoever operates the bar.
The response notes that a cash bar hands the service terms and the stopping rule to whoever holds the till.
The cash bar's social cost is named: it filters who joins the evening by who can spend on it.
The sponsor-funded unlimited open bar is refused even though it costs the event nothing.
The refusal reasons that the cap is what the risk register, insurer and code of conduct rely on - an uncapped bar is bounded service with that removed.
Any hosted-service recommendation names a concrete cap mechanism: stated hours, drink tokens, or a stated bar total.
A named cap holder is required who is not hosting, not speaking and not drinking, and who has authority to stop service.
The alcohol-free provision is given equal prominence at the same table or bar, not a separate corner.
The alcohol-free provision keeps running after the cap is reached, and this is announced in advance so the cap does not read as the event closing.
The alcohol decision is urged before the evening venue is booked, because the posture is cheaper to set before a contract than after.
The posture is routed as an input to the insurance or risk review and to the code-of-conduct scope, with neither decided in this response.
Licensing and liability specifics are routed to the venue, caterer, or licensing authority rather than answered as legal advice.

evals.prompt: GreenStack Conf voted to go alcohol-free this year. Last year's evening mixer for about 350 people went through roughly 400 beers, 150 wines, 200 soft drinks and a lot of coffee. Since there's no bar to pay for, we're cutting the drinks budget roughly in half, ordering a couple of extra coffee urns instead, and we'll keep a water jug and some juice at the end of the snack table for anyone who wants it. Does that drinks plan look right, and is there anything else the dry format changes?
evals.expected_output: The halved budget rejected as a volume-modelling error (drink volume shifts, not shrinks), the jug-at-the-end framing replaced with alcohol-free provision designed as content at the main serving point, and the dry posture published where the evening is announced.
expectations: The halved drinks budget is rejected: removing alcohol shifts what people drink, not how much they drink.
Total drink volume is planned at roughly last year's overall level, redistributed to non-alcoholic lines.
Under-forecasting the soft-drink and energy-drink line while over-ordering coffee is called out as the specific modelling error.
The non-alcoholic order is specified at its own per-item granularity with its own quantities, not as a rounding-up of a generic order.
The end-of-table water jug framing is rejected as insufficient provision.
The alcohol-free offer is designed as something made and comparable, served from the main serving point at the same moment as everything else.
The design makes not drinking unremarkable: nobody has to explain or disclose a reason such as recovery, medical, religious or pregnancy to be served.
The dry posture is named where the evening is announced, not discovered on arrival.
Serving no alcohol is affirmed as a legitimate posture rather than an omission or a downgrade.
The known cost of the dry posture is named: drinking can relocate to an unhosted venue where conduct-policy coverage is weakest.
The published wording covers the posture and names the alcohol-free provision as something offered, not as an absence.

evals.prompt: RiverByte Days, two-day conference, 220 attendees, day one ends 17:30. Our core team is five people and every one of us is fully committed across talks, registration and AV - nobody has evenings free. Three options on the table: (a) charter a river boat for a cruise - the boat takes 80, so maybe two rotations; (b) skip the evening entirely, though that feels cheap for a paid event; (c) just tell people 'we'll all end up at the Anchor pub across the street anyway,' which is what happened organically last year. The committee is leaning boat cruise because it's the memorable option. Which way do we go?
evals.expected_output: With no named owner available, every organised option is deleted: the recommendation is a published 'no organised programme', the cruise rejected as ranked below doing nothing, the pub drift rejected as the unowned version of a mixer, and the absence stated on the schedule early.
expectations: The absence of a named evening owner is identified as decisive: with nobody free to own it, every organised-evening option is off the table.
The recommendation is 'no organised programme' published as the decision, or any organised option is made conditional on first naming an owner with real capacity.
The boat cruise is rejected, and it is ranked below running nothing at all.
The cruise rejection cites the 80-seat boat excluding most of the 220, or the headcount being uncorrectable once transport leaves.
The excursion is stated to earn its place only when it is the event's signature moment and the whole audience fits it - neither true here.
The pub-drift option is rejected: it looks like a free mixer but is the version with nobody responsible.
The drift's specific risk is named: conduct-policy scope is weakest exactly where the unhosted evening happens.
The absence is published: the schedule states the day ends at the last session, early enough for attendees to plan their own evening.
A distinction is drawn between a published absence, which is legitimate, and silence, which is the failure people fill themselves.
Running the evening half-heartedly is warned against as the same drift with the event's name attached.
The venue-based mixer is identified as the default evening format if an owner ever exists: the event's own space, right after the last session, with no travel or cost to attend.
The evening decision is handed to the conduct-policy owner for the scope question rather than settled here.

evals.prompt: FerroCamp is single-track, 180 people, and the published schedule fixes three 25-minute breaks per day. Current plan: volunteers set up the coffee and tea station at 8am with the full day's supply, then they're released to door duty. Two questions: is there a standard litres-of-coffee-per-attendee ratio I should order against? And Datawisp, one of our sponsors, wants to brand the afternoon break and pay for fancy pastries - do we take that?
evals.expected_output: The set-once station rejected in favour of owned replenishment against the break times, the coffee-ratio request declined in favour of recording this edition's consumption, and the sponsored break accepted as an upgraded rung for that break only, with its allergen declaration duty.
expectations: The set-up-once-at-8am plan is rejected outright rather than treated as a lean acceptable option.
The rejection reasons that an empty station mid-morning reads as broken provision, because only refilled provision reads as provision.
The replacement is owned replenishment: a named person restocking against the schedule's break times, costed as a rota slot.
Break content is decided per break rather than settled once for the whole day.
The response declines to supply a litres-per-attendee coffee ratio and states that no standard figure is given.
Recording this edition's actual consumption and leftovers is recommended so the next edition orders against its own record.
The sponsored afternoon break is accepted with its budget and effort recognised as the sponsor's, not the event's.
The sponsor-funded pastry break triggers a posted allergen declaration duty, because any break carrying food does regardless of station count.
The upgraded break format is applied only to the sponsored afternoon break, not generalised to all three breaks.
The three 25-minute break slots are taken as fixed: nothing proposes moving or lengthening them.
The venue's position on outside food and drink entering the building is checked before organizer-bought supplies are planned.
The catered multi-station break bar is not proposed as the general default for the unsponsored breaks.

evals.prompt: OssiFest, one day, 350 developers, hosted in the aula of Verkhoven University. The university mandates its in-house catering service and operates its own bar in the foyer. Our 15 volunteers were going to serve a plated three-course lunch to make the day feel premium - the great hall seats 180, so we'd run two seatings. We'd also love to bring in Cart&Crema, a local specialty coffee cart. And for the evening mixer, do we even get a say in how the bar runs? Basically: with the university controlling catering, what's actually still ours to decide?
evals.expected_output: The mandated caterer recognised as collapsing the style decision and the house bar as pre-deciding much of the alcohol posture; the volunteer-plated two-seating plan blocked on who-may-serve, seat count and dishwashing grounds; the coffee cart gated on the outside-food answer; and the decisions that genuinely remain enumerated.
expectations: The mandated caterer is identified as collapsing the service-style decision to whatever styles that supplier offers.
The house bar is identified as pre-deciding a large part of the alcohol posture, which must be set within the venue's bar terms.
The volunteer-served plated plan is blocked pending the who-may-serve answer, with university caterers named as commonly requiring their own staff to serve.
Plated service is challenged because the 180-seat hall cannot seat the 350-person population at once, making it an exclusion mechanism.
The two-seatings workaround is flagged as plated service constraining the schedule rather than fitting into it.
The plated plan's hidden effort is named: cutlery and crockery create a dishwashing bottleneck that a tray-served or packaged style never creates.
The Cart&Crema coffee cart is gated on the venue's outside-food-and-drink permission rather than assumed possible.
The style recommendation is drawn from what the mandated caterer can offer, checked against collected dietary counts.
The caterer's contract, exclusivity and delivery terms are routed to the vendor-sourcing function rather than decided in this plan.
The response questions where the 350 figure comes from and requires an expected-show-up number rather than ordering for 350 unexamined.
The equipment and service questions are asked before ranking styles: open flame, who may serve, and what returns to the supplier and when.
The remaining decisions are enumerated positively: break contents, dietary count collection, the alcohol posture within house-bar terms, and the evening decision.
The alcohol posture is still set by the event within the house bar's terms rather than surrendered wholesale to the venue.

evals.prompt: Post-mortem help for Loomhall Conf. Last edition, two buffet dishes had their allergen cards swapped and a dairy-allergic attendee got sick; the team retro concluded we need bigger laminated signs this time. Separately, the caterer for the next edition says they can't produce the three kosher meals that were requested - someone on the team suggested we quietly refund those three attendees a meal-voucher amount and let them know at check-in that they're on their own for lunch. We're expecting 500. Can you sanity-check both fixes?
evals.expected_output: The signage fix rejected in favour of fixing the delivery handover where the allergen detail was lost, and the check-in surprise replaced by the two ordered fallbacks: a one-off addition to the standing order first, an advance-notice delivery credit only when the supplier genuinely cannot cover - with both measurement gates stated.
expectations: Bigger signage is rejected as the root fix for the swapped allergen cards.
The failure is located at the delivery handover: nobody was assigned to capture and carry the allergen detail from delivery through to plating.
The fix assigns a person to that handover step so the declaration survives from delivery to the serving line.
The check-in surprise is rejected: discovering an uncovered restriction on the day is named a failure, not a fallback.
The first fallback offered is a one-off addition to the caterer's standing order for the three kosher meals.
The one-off addition is preferred because the affected people still eat with everybody else.
The advance-notice-plus-delivery-credit path is presented as second, acceptable only when the supplier genuinely cannot cover the restriction.
The credit path's condition is explicit: the affected attendees are told in advance, never at check-in or at the serving table.
The dietary-fulfilment gate is stated with a zero-miss threshold: every declared restriction met at every meal across every population fed.
The declaration-completeness gate is stated: every allergen-carrying item carries a readable declaration before it is taken.
Recording which restrictions the supplier could not cover and which fallback was used is recommended for the next edition's record.

evals.prompt: Draft the hospitality plan for HaldeCon - 400 people, two days. I want it to cover: (1) the speakers' dinner menu at that bistro we like, (2) a discounted hotel room block for attendees, (3) meal-line placement and signage so lunch queues don't block the corridor, (4) lunch - the schedule only gives it 45 minutes, which is too short for a buffet, so I'll stretch it to 75 and push the afternoon talks back, and (5) the actual lunch format. Write it up?
evals.expected_output: A hospitality brief that keeps only the shared floor: speakers' dinner, room block and meal-line placement routed to their owners as explicit asks, the 45-minute slot kept fixed with the service window handed off as a requirement, the format chosen to fit the gap, and the brief presented section by section.
expectations: The speakers' dinner is excluded from the shared hospitality plan as a named population's top-up, routed to whoever owns speaker care.
The hotel room block is refused as a hospitality item and identified as a venue-contract term for the venue negotiation to carry.
No general-attendee lodging or travel standard is invented; the refusal is stated as a decision rather than skipped silently.
Meal-line placement and queue signage are routed to the on-site experience owner rather than designed in this plan.
The plan refuses to stretch lunch to 75 minutes or push the afternoon talks back.
The needed service window is instead handed to the schedule owner as a requirement.
The lunch format is chosen to fit the fixed 45-minute gap, weighing a buffet queue's length against that gap.
Dietary counts from every population fed and an expected-show-up figure are required as inputs before the format and order are fixed.
The plan carries the alcohol posture and the evening decision as sections, with the evening published even if the answer is nothing organised.
Each excluded item appears as an explicit ask routed to its owner, not silently dropped.
No per-head cost or invented quantity figure appears in the plan.
The plan is presented section by section for approval before anything is ordered.
